items.stem: Writes in an Azure Cosmos DB container are concentrating on one logical partition, throttling throughput. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: A partition key with low cardinality creating a hot partition
options.rationale: Correct: a poorly chosen, low-cardinality key funnels load to one partition.

options.text: Using the .NET SDK instead of the Python SDK
options.rationale: SDK choice does not cause hot partitions.

options.text: Enabling Time to Live on items
options.rationale: TTL expires items; it does not concentrate writes.
Consistency level does not determine partition distribution.

items.explanation: Correct: a poorly chosen, low-cardinality key funnels load to one partition.

items.stem: Which capability best supports retrieving semantically similar documents for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pattern in Azure Cosmos DB?

options.text: Vector search over a vector index
options.rationale: Correct: vector search finds nearest-neighbour embeddings for semantic retrieval.
Unique key policies enforce uniqueness, not semantic similarity.

options.text: A composite index for ORDER BY
options.rationale: Composite indexes speed ordering/filtering, not embedding similarity.
TTL controls item expiry, not retrieval relevance.

items.explanation: Correct: vector search finds nearest-neighbour embeddings for semantic retrieval.

items.stem: Which TWO actions improve availability of an Azure Cosmos DB solution? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: multi-region writes let the app write to the nearest region and survive regional loss.
Correct: automatic failover promotes a healthy region when one becomes unavailable.

options.text: Lower throughput to the minimum RU/s
options.rationale: Reducing RU/s risks throttling and does not improve availability.
Disabling indexing affects query cost, not availability.

options.text: Set consistency to strong in a single region
options.rationale: Single-region strong consistency does not improve regional availability.

items.explanation: Correct: multi-region writes let the app write to the nearest region and survive regional loss. Correct: automatic failover promotes a healthy region when one becomes unavailable.
